laws.rule: Beijing Capital and Beijing Daxing airports are 240-hour visa-free transit ports; the permitted area is all of Beijing.
Smartraveller notes a ban on drone use in Beijing in particular.

Smoking is banned in indoor public places, indoor workplaces and on public transport (article 9). The ban also covers the outdoor areas of kindergartens, schools, children's welfare sites, heritage sites open to the public, the competition and seating areas of sports grounds, and women's and children's hospitals (article 10). A person who smokes in a banned place or in a queue is ordered to stop and can be fined; near children's venues a warning and a fine apply (article 25).
laws.penalty_signal: In a place mainly used by children: warning, and a fine of CNY 200 to 500 (about A$42.66 to A$107) may follow. In other banned places or queues: CNY 50 (about A$10.67), rising to CNY 200 (about A$42.66) if the person does not stop. (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
laws.heading: 北京市控制吸烟条例 (Beijing Tobacco Control Regulation)

laws.rule: Spitting or urinating in public, dropping cigarette butts, paper or plastic, writing or scribbling on public buildings and facilities, and smoking in banned places or queues are listed as uncivilised behaviour to be policed (article 27). Dog owners must keep dogs on a lead and clear the droppings, and e-bikes may not be charged in shared corridors, stairwells or exits (article 30). For tourists, scratching or defacing heritage sites and tourist facilities, digging up or picking plants in scenic areas, and hurting or wrongly feeding animals are listed (article 31). The regulation itself sets no fine amounts: article 56 sends the penalty to other laws, including the Public Security Administration Punishments Law and Beijing's Tobacco Control Regulation.
laws.penalty_signal: Penalty set by the other laws named in article 56; not stated in this regulation.
laws.heading: 北京市文明行为促进条例 (Beijing Civilised Behaviour Promotion Regulation)

laws.rule: Setting off fireworks is banned inside the Fifth Ring Road (including the road itself) (article 14). It is also banned at and around heritage sites, stations, airports, hospitals, kindergartens, schools, aged care homes, forests and other listed sites (article 13), and while the orange or red air-pollution alert is on (article 15). Districts outside the Fifth Ring Road can ban or restrict it by area and time.
laws.penalty_signal: For an individual: CNY 100 to 200 (about A$21.33 to A$42.66), and CNY 200 to 500 (about A$42.66 to A$107) in serious cases; fireworks are seized (article 21). (CNY at 4.6877 per A$1, RBA 30 Oct 2026.)
